questions.question: Who was the Anglo-Norman noblewoman who commissioned Geoffrei Gaimar around 1136 to compose 'L'Estoire des Engleis'?
questions.explanation: Constance FitzGilbert of Lincolnshire commissioned Gaimar to translate historical sources into Anglo-Norman French verse.

questions.question: To which English queen consort and patron of troubadour culture was Wace's 1155 verse romance 'Roman de Brut' dedicated?
questions.explanation: Wace presented his French octosyllabic verse adaptation of Geoffrey of Monmouth to Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine around 1155.

questions.question: In which Worcestershire parish did the poet-priest Layamon live and serve while composing his Middle English alliterative 'Brut'?
questions.explanation: In the prologue of his Brut, Layamon identifies himself as a priest residing at Ernley, now known as Areley Kings on the Severn.

questions.question: What specific metrical form was adopted by Anglo-Norman poets such as Wace and Marie de France for their verse narratives?
questions.explanation: Anglo-Norman romances, lais, and chronicles predominantly utilized rhymed octosyllabic couplets derived from continental French verse.

questions.question: What technical linguistic label is given by scholars to the Early Middle English dialect found in 'Ancrene Wisse' and MS Bodley 34?
questions.explanation: J.R.R. Tolkien identified the remarkably consistent West Midland literary dialect shared by Ancrene Wisse and the Katherine Group as AB language.

questions.question: Which 12th-century Latin theological treatise by Hugh of Saint Victor serves as the source for the Middle English allegory 'Sawles Warde'?
questions.explanation: Sawles Warde is an Early Middle English homiletic adaptation of parts of Hugh of Saint Victor's treatise De Anima.

questions.question: In the allegorical text 'Sawles Warde', which personified faculty represents the master of the house of the human body?
questions.explanation: Wit represents the rational master of the household, who must maintain discipline over his unruly wife Will and bodily senses.

questions.question: In the allegorical structure of 'Sawles Warde', which figure is cast as Wit's headstrong and disorderly wife?
questions.explanation: In Sawles Warde, Will personifies the appetites and passions that constantly threaten to overpower Wit's rational governance.

questions.question: Which prose treatise in the Katherine Group vigorously argues that virginity is far superior to the domestic burdens of marriage?
questions.explanation: Hali Meidhad, or Holy Maidenhood, is an early 13th-century prose tract warning women against marriage and childbirth trials.

questions.question: Which famous Oxford manuscript preserves the five early 13th-century devotional texts known collectively as the Katherine Group?
questions.explanation: MS Bodley 34 in the Bodleian Library is the primary manuscript preserving the Katherine Group virgin martyr legends and tracts.

questions.question: To which specific historical arbitrator do the disputing birds in 'The Owl and the Nightingale' agree to submit their debate?
questions.explanation: At the close of The Owl and the Nightingale, the birds travel to Dorset to seek the verdict of Master Nicholas of Guildford.

questions.question: In which Dorset settlement is Master Nicholas of Guildford said to dwell in 'The Owl and the Nightingale'?
questions.explanation: The poem praises Master Nicholas and specifies that he lives in the rural village of Portisham in Dorset.

questions.question: Which Oxford manuscript contains the oldest and finest surviving Anglo-Norman text of the epic 'The Song of Roland'?
questions.explanation: Bodleian Library MS Digby 23, copied in an Anglo-Norman hand in England around 1125 to 1150, preserves the primary text of Roland.

questions.question: In which dialect and insular script was the celebrated Oxford Digby 23 manuscript of 'The Song of Roland' penned?
questions.explanation: The Oxford Roland is written in the Anglo-Norman dialect of French, demonstrating the insular preservation of French epics.

questions.question: Which 12th-century writer composed the earliest known surviving Anglo-Norman poem, a scientific calendar treatise titled 'Comput'?
questions.explanation: Philippe de Thaon composed his Comput around 1119, followed by his Bestiaire dedicated to Queen Adeliza of Louvain.

questions.question: Which queen consort of King Henry I served as the royal literary patron for Philippe de Thaon's Anglo-Norman 'Bestiaire'?
questions.explanation: Philippe de Thaon explicitly dedicated his verse Bestiaire around 1121 to Queen Adeliza, second wife of Henry I.

questions.question: Into how many distinct thematic books or parts is the prose devotional guide 'Ancrene Wisse' divided?
questions.explanation: Ancrene Wisse is structured into eight books, with Books 1 and 8 forming the Outer Rule and Books 2 to 7 the Inner Rule.

questions.question: In Book Seven of 'Ancrene Wisse', what prominent allegorical parable illustrates Christ's redemption of the human soul?
options: A King wooing an imprisoned lady
A Knight storming a dragon's cave
questions.explanation: Christ is allegorized as a noble King who woos an ungrateful lady besieged in an earthen castle, dying to save her.

questions.question: Which Anglo-Norman poet wrote a vivid, eyewitness verse chronicle in rhyming alexandrines on the Scottish war of 1173 to 1174?
questions.explanation: Jordan Fantosme, a cleric of Winchester, composed a firsthand chronicle of the northern campaign against King William the Lion.

questions.question: Which northern English chronicler translated Pierre de Langtoft's Anglo-Norman verse chronicle into Middle English couplets in 1338?
questions.explanation: Robert Mannyng completed his English Chronicle of England in 1338, adapting Langtoft's Anglo-Norman chronicle for the second part.

questions.question: Which 12th-century Anglo-Welsh cleric and archdeacon of Brecon authored 'Topographia Hibernica' and 'Itinerarium Kambriae'?
questions.explanation: Giraldus Cambrensis, or Gerald of Wales, wrote ethnographic and topographical accounts of Ireland and Wales in elegant Latin.

questions.question: Which 12th-century English historian popularized the famous anecdote of King Canute rebuking the incoming ocean tide?
questions.explanation: Henry of Huntingdon recorded the didactic story of King Canute demonstrating the limits of royal power in his Historia Anglorum.

questions.question: In 'Historia Anglorum', Henry of Huntingdon structures British history around five invasions: Romans, Saxons, Danes, Normans, and which fifth group?
questions.explanation: Henry of Huntingdon listed the five scourges of Britain as the Romans, the Scots and Picts, the English, the Danes, and the Normans.

questions.question: To which powerful royal figure, the Earl of Gloucester and illegitimate son of Henry I, did Geoffrey of Monmouth dedicate his history?
questions.explanation: Geoffrey of Monmouth dedicated his Historia Regum Britanniae to Robert, Earl of Gloucester, a pre-eminent Anglo-Norman magnate.

questions.question: According to Geoffrey of Monmouth's legendary history, which exiled Trojan hero conquered Britain and founded New Troy?
questions.explanation: Geoffrey traced Britain's founding to Brutus, great-grandson of Aeneas, who purged the island of giants and founded Troia Nova.

questions.question: What is the name of the fateful battlefield where King Arthur and Mordred slay each other, as recorded by Geoffrey of Monmouth?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Camlann, placed around 537 or 542 in legend, marks Arthur's final clash where Mordred is killed and Arthur is wounded.

questions.question: The Anglo-Norman verse romance of 'Tristran' composed around 1170 by Thomas of Britain represents which literary aesthetic?
questions.explanation: Thomas of Britain wrote the refined, courtly psychological version of Tristan, emphasizing emotional introspection and chivalric decorum.

questions.question: Which Middle High German poet composed his celebrated Arthurian romance 'Tristan und Isold' by adapting Thomas of Britain's Anglo-Norman poem?
questions.explanation: Gottfried von Strassburg explicitly named Thomas of Britain as his master source for his classic German verse Tristan.

questions.question: In Marie de France's lai 'Guigemar', which creature inflicts a wound on the hero and foretells his suffering for love?
questions.explanation: Guigemar wounds an enchanted white doe, whose rebounded arrow wounds his thigh while the beast curses him to suffer for love.

questions.question: In Marie de France's lai 'Les Deus Amanz', what arduous physical challenge must the young lover perform to win his lady's hand?
options: Carry her up a high mountain without resting
questions.explanation: The youth carries his beloved up a steep Norman mountain, refusing to drink a strengthening potion until his heart bursts at the summit.

questions.question: Which lai by Marie de France tells of a fairy lover who visits an imprisoned lady by flying through her window in the shape of a hawk?
questions.explanation: Muldumarec transforms into a hawk to visit the locked-away lady, fathering the hero Yonec who later avenges his parents.

questions.question: In Marie de France's lai 'Laustic', what object is kept in a jewel-encrusted casket by the knight to remember his thwarted love?
questions.explanation: After the lady's jealous husband wrings the nightingale's neck, the knight has the bird embalmed in a golden vessel.

questions.question: Which lai by Marie de France portrays a noble knight whose self-sacrificing first wife, Guildeluec, enters a convent to allow his remarriage?
questions.explanation: In Eliduc, Guildeluec graciously accepts holy vows upon realizing her husband's deep love for the foreign princess Guilliadun.

questions.question: What is the title of Marie de France's collection of 102 fables translated into Anglo-Norman verse from an English source?
questions.explanation: Marie de France compiled Ysopet, or Little Aesop, claiming in her epilogue to translate an English book compiled by King Alfred.

questions.question: Which narrative poem by Marie de France describes the descent of an Irish knight, Owein, into an entrance of purgatory?
questions.explanation: Marie adapted the Latin vision of Saint Patrick's Purgatory into Anglo-Norman verse, describing knight Owein's spiritual trials.

questions.question: Which Anglo-Norman outlaw romance depicts the historical Marcher baron who rebelled against King John in Shropshire and the Welsh border?
questions.explanation: Fouke le Fitz Waryn combines historical chronicle and romance, detailing Fulk III FitzWarin's guerilla rebellion against King John.

questions.question: Which landmark 1258 state document, reforming baronial government under Henry III, was the first royal proclamation issued in English since 1066?
questions.explanation: The Provisions of Oxford in 1258 were circulated in Latin, French, and English, marking the re-emergence of written English for state use.

questions.question: Which English monarch was forced by Simon de Montfort and the barons to accept the Provisions of Oxford in 1258?
questions.explanation: Henry III conceded governmental authority to a baronial council of fifteen under the revolutionary Provisions of Oxford in 1258.

questions.question: The moral treatise 'Ayenbite of Inwit' is celebrated by historical linguists as the quintessential specimen of which Middle English dialect?
questions.explanation: Dan Michel's 1340 autograph manuscript provides an invaluable, localized phonetic record of the fourteenth-century Kentish dialect.

questions.question: Which French Dominican friar authored 'La Somme des Vices et des Vertus', the primary source translated into 'Ayenbite of Inwit'?
questions.explanation: Friar Laurent of Orleans composed Somme le Roi in 1279 for King Philip III of France, which Dan Michel translated into English.

questions.question: What is the title of William of Wadington's 13th-century Anglo-Norman work that Robert Mannyng translated into 'Handlyng Synne'?
questions.explanation: Mannyng translated the Anglo-Norman Manuel des Pechiez, expanding its didactic stories into vigorous English verse.

questions.question: Which poem, composed around 1170 in septenary couplets, represents the earliest surviving Middle English rhymed poem?
questions.explanation: Poema Morale, or the Moral Ode, consists of around 400 lines of rhyming fourteeners advising listeners to repent and avoid damnation.

questions.question: What is the strict metrical pattern devised by Orm for his 'Ormulum', consisting of unrhymed fifteen-syllable verses?
questions.explanation: The Ormulum uses unrhymed iambic septenaries of fifteen syllables with an unvarying midline caesura after the eighth syllable.

questions.question: To which fellow Augustinian canon and brother in the flesh did Orm dedicate his monumental verse work 'The Ormulum'?
questions.explanation: In the dedication of the Ormulum, Orm addresses his brother Walter as his brother in the flesh and brother in Christ.

questions.question: In 'Havelok the Dane', what miraculous bodily phenomenon reveals Havelok's royal Danish parentage while he sleeps?
options: A deep scar across his forehead
A brilliant flame shining from his mouth
A sweet fragrance from his hands
A glowing halo above his head
questions.explanation: A bright light streaming from Havelok's mouth and a royal birthmark on his shoulder prove his legitimate royal lineage.

questions.question: What is the name of the disinherited English princess whom Havelok the Dane marries and restores to the throne of England?
questions.explanation: Princess Goldborough, daughter of King Athelwold, is imprisoned by the treacherous Godrich until Havelok rescues and marries her.

questions.question: At which English Benedictine abbey was the famous Harley MS 978 containing the musical rota 'Sumer is icumen in' written and preserved?
questions.explanation: The rota Sumer is icumen in was recorded around 1250 in the scriptorium of Reading Abbey in Berkshire.

questions.question: What is the title of the fragmentary 12th-century Anglo-Norman drama that dramatizes Christ's burial and the harrowing of hell?
questions.explanation: La Seinte Resureccion, surviving in fragments in Paris and London manuscripts, is a pioneer vernacular passion and Easter play.

questions.question: In 'Le Mystere d'Adam', while the spoken dialogue of the actors is in Anglo-Norman French, in what language are the rubrics written?
questions.explanation: The extensive stage directions and choral responsories in Le Mystere d'Adam are written in liturgical church Latin.

questions.question: Which late 14th-century English poet authored 'Sir Launfal', an expanded Middle English tail-rhyme adaptation of Marie de France's 'Lanval'?
questions.explanation: Thomas Chestre composed Sir Launfal, adapting Marie de France's lai into a popular 12-line tail-rhyme English romance.
